identity.title: Reduction of the maximum mass-loss rate of OH/IR stars due to unnoticed binary interaction

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here, we report on the detection of spiral structures around two cornerstone extreme OH/IR-stars, OH 26.5+0.6 and OH 30.1$-$0.7, identifying them as wide binary systems.

evidence.loc: Derived mass-loss rates for extreme OH/IR-stars

question.value: Why do extreme OH/IR stars appear to have a very short (~200-1000 yr) high mass-loss superwind phase, and what is the maximum AGB mass-loss rate?

evidence.loc: abstract
evidence.quote: A condundrum arises whereby the observationally determined duration of the superwind phase is too short for these stars to become white dwarfs

findings_qualitative.value: Incomplete ring-like patterns and PV diagrams reveal binary-induced shell-like spirals in both stars

evidence.quote: The PV diagrams prove that the circumstellar envelope of both targets is shaped by a *binary-induced shell-like spiral*

claims.hypothesis: Are extreme OH/IR stars binaries whose companions mimic a short superwind?
claims.experiment: ALMA 12CO channel maps and PV diagrams compared with binary hydrodynamic models
claims.result: Spiral/ring patterns detected; CEDE with ~10x density contrast
claims.finding: Short superwind duration is an artefact of a binary-induced CEDE

evidence.loc: abstract
evidence.quote: Hydrodynamical simulations show that the companion’s gravitational attraction creates an equatorial density enhancement mimicking a short extreme superwind phase

claims.hypothesis: What is the maximum AGB mass-loss rate?
claims.experiment: Argue that CO-based rates are reliable and dust-based rates overestimated
claims.finding: Maximum rate is near the single-scattering limit

evidence.loc: abstract
evidence.quote: This discovery restricts the maximum mass-loss rate of AGB stars around the single-scattering radiation-pressure limit of a few 10$^{-5}$ M$_{\odot}$/yr.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA data cannot give the companion mass

evidence.loc: Binary properties of OH 26.5+0.6 and OH 30.1$-$0.7
evidence.quote: The current ALMA data do not allow an accurate estimate of the companion’s mass.

referee_caveats_inferred: Simulations used were not tuned to these stars (primary 1.5 Msun)
Only two stars observed; generalisation to all extreme OH/IR stars is statistical
Binomial argument assumes independence and a 10,000 yr lifetime
